create.name: Keizan Scott Roshi
create.bio:
Keizan Scott Roshi (the Rev. Dr David Keizan Shoji Scott) founded and leads the StoneWater Zen Sangha, whose centre is on Hope Street in Liverpool. Before Zen he earned a doctorate at Manchester University, then spent time in Okinawa in the mid-1970s training in Uechi-ryu karate and brought that style back to Britain. He began Zen practice in 1982 in the White Plum lineage of Taizan Maezumi Roshi, first with Genpo Merzel and later with Tenshin Fletcher Roshi, who gave him Dharma transmission in 2009 and inka in 2019. He sits on the board of the White Plum Asanga and represents it in Europe.

His teaching follows the Soto emphasis on shikantaza, just sitting, alongside koan study and the Big Mind process, and several of his students have now received transmission from him. In Liverpool he leads sittings on Wednesday evenings and Saturday mornings with talks and one-to-one interviews, the sangha also sits together on Zoom, and twice a year he teaches week-long sesshin, usually at Crosby Hall on Merseyside. He has written widely on Japan and Zen, including The Way of Zen with Tenshin Fletcher and The Elements of Zen with Tony Shinro Doubleday, and many of his talks are free as a podcast.

books.title: The Way of Zen
books.author: David Scott
books.description: An introduction to Zen written with his own teacher, Tenshin Fletcher Roshi. It covers the history of the tradition, how zazen is practised and what training with a teacher involves.

books.title: The Elements of Zen
books.author: David Scott
books.description: A short beginner's book co-written with Tony Shinro Doubleday, who later became one of his Dharma heirs. It sets out the basic ideas and forms of Zen practice in plain terms.

books.title: Easy-to-use Zen
books.author: David Scott
books.description: A small practical handbook that brings Zen attitudes and simple sitting practice into ordinary daily life.

courses.title: Weekly zazen at the Liverpool zendo
courses.description: Regular sittings at the StoneWater centre on Hope Street every Wednesday evening and Saturday morning. Sessions include zazen, Dharma talks and private interviews with Roshi and the other teachers.

courses.title: StoneWater Online Zendo
courses.description: Zazen sessions held on Zoom for people who cannot get to Liverpool. There is no fee; the sangha asks those who keep coming to consider a donation towards its running costs.

courses.title: Spring Sesshin 2027
courses.description: The sangha's week-long spring retreat at Crosby Hall near Liverpool, its usual venue for many years. A sesshin centres on long periods of sitting and walking meditation with talks and interviews.

free_resources.title: StoneWater Zen Talks
free_resources.description: A free podcast of short Dharma talks, mostly Keizan Roshi speaking at the Hope Street zendo, with some recorded on retreat. Older talks are on the sangha's YouTube channel.

sprint.tier_evidence: No personal social accounts found. The StoneWater Zen YouTube channel @stonewaterzen930 shows 307 subscribers (channel header, 3 Nov 2026) but is the sangha's shared channel, so not counted; sangha Facebook and Twitter not readable without logging in → 0 readable → local_hero
flags: Named 'Keizan Scott Roshi' (Roshi kept as part of how he is known, as with Ajahn/Bhante); slug keizan-scott. His books are published as David Scott.

Email stonewaterzenbooking@gmail.com is the sangha's retreat-booking inbox (handled by Stephan Shigetsu), published on the event dates page; the site's general route is a contact form (https://www.stonewaterzen.org/contact/).

Base: the StoneWater Zen Centre at Hope Street, Liverpool (contact page) and his biography, which describes him returning to Liverpool and holding his transmission ceremony there; recorded as Liverpool.
Videos are on the sangha's shared YouTube channel (stonewaterzen), all Dharma talks given by him, recorded 2017-2018 when he was titled Sensei; youtube_url points at that shared channel.

Spring Sesshin 2027 (4-10 April, Crosby Hall) is announced on the dates page with details 'to be posted toward the end of this year'; no price yet and the page does not name the teachers, though the autumn sesshin is described as led by Roshi and the other Sensei.
Several StoneWater pages still carry an old COVID closure banner while the same pages say the Liverpool zendo has reopened; the schedule was taken from the current Schedule (Liverpool) page.

Books confirmed on Open Library by the ISBNs on the sangha's own reading list: https://openlibrary.org/isbn/0312206208 , https://openlibrary.org/isbn/1862040427 (listed there as 'Zen (Elements of... Series)') , https://openlibrary.org/isbn/1843335875 .
He is in his later years; the site shows him active (2026 transmission ceremonies, current schedule), but a human may want to confirm he still teaches weekly.
Ingest check notes a different book titled 'The Way of Zen' (Alan Watts) already in the database; this is the Scott and Fletcher book, added anyway.
left_out: Cookery and travel books (Three Bowl Cookbook, Japanese Cooking, Samurai and Cherry Blossom, Essential Japan, Japan AA Explorer), The Fighting Arts (martial arts) and Simply Zen (interiors and gardens): outside spiritual teaching.

Talks on the channel by other teachers (Tenshin Fletcher Roshi, Shinro Doubleday, shuso ceremonies).
